hook: Karen rings the smart doorbell 47 times screaming for the homeowner
title: 🤖 Doorbell SPRAYED Karen! 😂 #Shorts
prompt:
Vertical 9:16 short, exactly 10 seconds, 30fps. Raw CCTV / dashcam / smart-camera aesthetic: high contrast, slightly desaturated daylight, timestamp HUD overlay in the top corner (e.g. 'CAM 03 - 14:22:07'). No black bars, no watermark, no cinematic letterbox.

Cast: Karen: middle-aged white woman, blonde bob or messy bun, oversized sunglasses pushed up on her head, pink tracksuit top. Perpetually outraged: wide eyes, mouth open mid-rant, finger jabbing. AI device: a smart doorbell — an EVERYDAY automated friction point, not a studio prop. Anthropomorphized just enough: glowing status light and a small screen face showing deadpan text. The AI device stays perfectly calm while Karen escalates — its comedy comes from cold literal enforcement, never arguing back. One bystander frozen mid-stare, phone out, selling the 'caught on camera' realism.

0-2s COLD COLLISION HOOK (conflict already in progress, zero setup): Karen rings the smart doorbell 47 times screaming for the homeowner. SENSORY hook, not narrative — the swipe decision happens in 200-500ms, so frame 1 leads with visual incongruity / motion delta (red pulse, LED flash, Karen mid-lunge) before any story. Giant ALL-CAPS text overlay in the first second, 6 words max, stating the absurdity. Visual jolt in second 1-2 — movement in every frame, nothing static. UI SAFE ZONE (hard rule): every key text overlay and the visual gag MUST sit in the top-middle third of the frame. NEVER place critical info on the right edge (engagement icons cover it) or in the bottom 25% (Shorts title/channel overlay truncates it). CCTV timestamp HUD goes top-LEFT corner only.

2-6.5s RAPID ESCALATION: Karen pushes the doorbell to its limit — the exact wrong move, louder, closer to camera, absurd demand. The doorbell responds with cold literal logic: it does not argue, it ENFORCES. Deadpan 0.5s pause before it acts — the pause IS the joke.

6.5-7.5s CLIMAX — SUDDEN PHYSICAL KARMA (the punchline window, highest-leverage second): sudden physical consequence in under 2 seconds — the smart doorbell sprayeds Karen (tangible: spray, lock, trap, soak). Karen left defeated on camera. The consequence MUST land inside 6.5-7.5s and be TANGIBLE and SUDDEN — spray, lock, trap, soak, tow — never a purely verbal burn. Karen defeated: slumped, silent, soaked, or escorted past the camera.

7.5-9s LOOP-OUT (max ~2s aftermath, then hard cut): AI chimes a reset phrase ('NEXT CUSTOMER, PLEASE.') matching the opening audio/frame. Final frame MUST visually rhyme with frame 1 (same angle on the doorbell, Karen re-entering) — post-generation verified by loop_check.py (similarity >= 0.85). No dead air: cut the moment the karma lands + 2s.

Audio (retention anchor): second 0 opens with ONE crisp Foley transient (glass crack, horn blip, sharp gasp) — preferably a mute-drop (sudden ambient hush) INTO the hit. SFX over music beds: naturalistic Foley + low CCTV current-hum, mobile-safe dynamic range, no clipping. NEVER a loud royalty-free upbeat track, NEVER harsh alarm blasts, NEVER silent for more than 1 second. On-screen text: max 3 overlays, each 6 words or fewer, ALL CAPS, yellow/white with black stroke, ALL inside the top-middle third of the frame (UI safe zone — never right edge or bottom 25%). CCTV timestamp HUD top-LEFT corner only. Burned-in subtitles for Karen's key rant line (60%+ watch muted). Hard cuts only — no slow motion, no fade-to-black, no static text-only openings. Karen ALWAYS loses; instant karma is the brand.
